name: 豆月 (Mamezuki)
gf_detail: The signature sweets are agar-and-bean based (黒豆かん, 豆しるこ) and many items are naturally wheat-free, but there is no documented gluten-free program, no dedicated equipment, and items like 餅 (mochi) and seasonal dishes vary. Not a celiac-safe destination; a celiac diner would need to ask about each item directly in Japanese.

name: 玄米菜食 明制（てんてん・野町） (Genmai Saishoku Meisei (Tenten Nomachi))
gf_detail: No gluten-free claim is documented. This is a brown-rice macrobiotic vegan kitchen, not a celiac-safe operation. Documented dishes include a soba (buckwheat) galette made with soy milk and soy-based meat alternatives, and Japanese plant-based cooking that typically relies on wheat-containing soy sauce. There is no mention of gluten-free soy sauce, a dedicated fryer, or cross-contamination controls

name: グリーンノート（光明食養研究所） (Green Note (Komyo Shokuyo Kenkyusho))
neighborhood: 瓢箪町 (Hyotanmachi), near Omicho Market and Hashiba-cho, centr
